q: The study of plant diseases is called plant _____. (2025- Set 12)
e: Pathology is the branch of science concerned with the study of plant diseases.

q: Biotic diseases are caused by _____. (2025- Set 7)
e: Biotic plant diseases are caused by living organism pathogens.

q: Plant disease is any _____ condition that alters the appearance or function of a plant. (2025- Set 10)
e: Plant disease is defined as any abnormal condition altering normal plant structure or function.

q: Plant disease is a _____ process that affects some or all plant functions. (2025- Set 5)
e: Plant disease represents a physiological process affecting plant functionality.

q: Most plant diseases, around _____ percent are caused by fungal or fungal like organisms. (2025- Set 1)
e: Fungi and fungal-like organisms account for approximately 85% of plant diseases.

q: Infectious plant diseases are caused by _____. (2025- Set 8)
e: Infectious plant diseases are transmitted by pathogenic organisms.

q: Plant _____ means a study of plant diseases. (2025- Set 2)
e: Plant pathology is specifically the study of diseases affecting plants.

q: Most plant diseases, around 85 percent are caused by _____ organisms. (2024-Set 3)
e: Around 85% of plant diseases are caused by fungal pathogens.

q: The study of plant diseases is called plant _____. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Plant pathology is defined as the scientific study of plant diseases.

q: Plant disease is caused by a _____ or an environmental factor. (2025- Set 9)
e: Plant diseases stem from either infectious pathogens or non-infectious environmental factors.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by _____ environmental condition. (2025- Set 6)
e: Abiotic diseases are non-infectious and result from non-living environmental stressors.

q: Signs of plant disease are _____ evidence of the pathogen. (2026- Set 1) (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများစုတွင်မေး)
e: Signs of plant disease refer to the visible physical presence of the pathogen.

q: Plant pathogens are very similar to those that cause _____ in humans and animals. (2026-Set 2)
e: Plant pathogens cause diseases in plants similarly to pathogens causing diseases in humans and animals.

q: Soft rot of fruits disease caused by _____. (2025- Set 11)
e: Rhizopus is a primary fungal pathogen causing soft rot in fruits.

q: _____ are intracellular pathogenic particles that infect other living organisms. (2024-Set 4) (2025-Set 13)
e: Viruses are obligate intracellular pathogenic particles.

q: Nematodes are simple, _____ animals. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Nematodes are simple multicellular roundworms.

q: Oxygen is supplied to the heart muscle by the _____. (2026- နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Coronary arteries deliver oxygenated blood to the heart muscle.

q: Sedentary lifestyle can lead to _____ diseases. (2026- Set 1)
e: Lack of physical activity in a sedentary lifestyle contributes to heart disease.

q: Examples of non-infectious diseases include _____. (2025- Set3)
e: Diabetes is a non-infectious metabolic disorder.

q: More white blood cells, lipids and connective tissue build up and harden to form a fibrous plaque called _____. (2025- Set6)
e: An atheroma is a fatty, fibrous plaque deposit inside artery walls.

q: A stroke is caused by an interruption to the normal blood supply to an area of the _____. (2025- Set 8, 10)
e: A stroke occurs when blood supply to a region of the brain is interrupted.

q: Antihypertensives drugs reduce the risk of damage to the kidneys and _____ from high blood pressure. (2025- Set 1)
e: Antihypertensive drugs lower blood pressure to prevent organ damage to the kidneys and eyes.

q: The myocardial infarction commonly known as a _____. (2024-Set 2)
e: Myocardial infarction is the medical term for a heart attack.

q: Smoking also changes the balance of _____ in the blood. (2024-Set 3)
e: Smoking alters the ratio and balance of lipoproteins circulating in the bloodstream.

q: Smoking also changes the balance of lipoproteins in the _____. (2025-Set 4)
e: Lipoprotein levels in the blood are negatively affected by smoking.

q: The female Anopheles mosquito is therefore a vector of _____. (2026- Set 2)
e: Female Anopheles mosquitoes serve as vectors that transmit malaria parasites.

q: Diseases that are always in populations are described as _____. (2025- Set 2)
e: An endemic disease is constantly present in a specific population or region.

q: Most cases of _____ are caused by Plasmodium. (2025- Set 3)
e: Malaria is caused by infection with Plasmodium parasites.

q: Female Anopheles mosquitoes feed on human blood to obtain the _____ they need to develop their eggs. (2025- Set 5, 7, 9)
e: Female mosquitoes require blood proteins for egg maturation.

q: Infectious disease includes _____. (2025- Set 12)
e: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infectious disease.

q: Quinine and chloroquine are used in the treatment of _____. (2025- Set 11)
e: Quinine and chloroquine are antimalarial medications.

q: Artesunate is a drug derived from the plant compound _____. (2025- Set 13)
e: Artesunate is a semisynthetic derivative of artemisinin.

q: An example of infectious diseases is _____. (2024-Set 4)
e: Malaria is an infectious vector-borne disease.

q: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in _____. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများစုတွင်မေး, နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Mosquitoes deposit their eggs in aquatic environments.

q: The best protection against malaria is _____. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Avoiding mosquito bites is the primary preventive measure against malaria transmission.
